main_text.l: Itala terrarum domitrix prætexitur ora,
Gallica perpetuo dum radens littora cursu,
Hesperiasque legens Eoi limitis urbes,
Herculeis qua porta patet suffulta columnis,
Oceani nostrum pelagus se mergit in Indas.
Quid plura? Europa superato limite, latos-
Sarmatiæ alterius campos, duce fretus eodem,
Ingredior, Scythicúque gelu: nec me Immanis ingen-
sNon Colchis, Chalybesque feri, nö ferrea claustra,
Non illa infames æterno frigore cautes-
Caucasea, Hircana aut tigres potuere morari-
Extremos hominum properantem visere Sinas,
Et sua ab arboribus pectentes vellera Seres,
India dein, medio findit quam gurgite Ganges,
Gedrosiique ingens disterminat Indus ab oris,
Perlustrata mihi, Brachmanū & turma sophorū.
Qu-
id gentes memorem innumeras? quid flumi-
na? montes?

volucrem Tigrin, contento qualis ab arcu-
Missa sagitta volat, curvata cortice cymba,

page.notes: Verse text in italic throughout; the headword "THEOD. BEZÆ" is the running head. Some words are uncertain in the long-s/f forms (e.g. "Sarmatiæ", "aßn", "Græsus") and in "Brachmanū"; the last line "Hinc" is a catchword. Dropped/ambiguous readings are marked as printed.
